title: When the Thorn Turns
premise: Coral Vane, a mercenary bound by an old oath to a god who stopped answering, has spent years keeping the ledgers of the Gilded Thorn, a guild that trades in impossible things—bottled grief, borrowed names, one-way doors. When prayers across the country of Vessia begin to be answered again, Coral learns his silent god was never dead but imprisoned, and that the guild's ledgers are the lock. To free it, he must find the Door of Unmaking—the only way out of Vessia, which officially ceased to exist when its borders were erased from every map and memory. In the end Coral pays the ledger's final price: he trades away his own name and history to open the door, freeing his god and his found family at the cost of being forgotten by everyone he loves—until one of them chooses to remember him anyway.
about_author: Zephyrine Oyelaran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trade records from vanished merchant cities before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about bureaucracy, belief, and the people who keep the books when empires fall.

chapters.title: The Weight of Blank Pages
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. He audits the Gilded Thorn's ledgers on the eve of the guild's centennial, noting entries that shouldn't exist—payments made in prayers. Establishes his dry competence and loneliness. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: A God Who Stopped Writing Back
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Flashback woven through present: the night eleven years ago his god, Vessel-of-Thorns, went silent mid-oath, leaving Coral's mercenary contract eternally unfinished. Beat: grief disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid in Memory
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A weeping woman trades her memory of her son for passage money; Coral processes the transaction and feels the first crack in his neutrality. Introduces guild mistress Sable Quill. Beat: complicity.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered in Vessia
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Across the city, shrines flare with light; impossible things grow cheap as gods start answering again. Sable panics—an economy built on divine silence is collapsing. Beat: fear of change.

chapters.title: Ledger Entries That Bleed
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The old ledgers begin writing themselves, ink surfacing like wounds. Each entry names a prayer answered—and a price extracted. Coral realizes the books are a prison mechanism. Beat: horrified discovery.

chapters.title: The Cartographer of Nowhere
chapters.summary: New character Ilex's POV—a disgraced mapmaker who remembers Vessia existed. She finds Coral because his name appears on a map that predates the erasure. Beat: reluctant alliance sparked by shared impossibility.

chapters.title: What the Guild Keeps in the Cellar
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. He descends into the Thorn's cellar and finds a door of black thornwood humming with his god's voice—faint, alive, imprisoned. Beat: hope arriving like an alarm bell.

chapters.title: Sable's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable confesses the guild's founding sin: they built the ledgers to cage the gods and monopolize the miraculous. She offers Coral partnership or silence. Beat: betrayal reframed as survival.

chapters.title: Found Family, Forged in Debt
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, rotating close-third. Coral, Ilex, and guild runner Pip—a child debtor—share a meal and trade stories of what they've lost. Beat: warmth taking root despite danger.

chapters.title: The Country That Was Deleted
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. She explains the Erasure: Vessia's borders were traded away generations ago; the Door of Unmaking is the only exit from a place that officially isn't there. Beat: vertigo of existential stakes.

chapters.title: First Prayer, First Price
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Pip prays impulsively for food and receives a feast—but a neighbor forgets Pip exists. The children of the guild learn what answering costs. Beat: innocence curdling.

chapters.title: Hunters of the Silent Order
chapters.summary: Antagonist introduction, High Warden Casserly's POV. The Silent Order, sworn to keep gods caged, arrives in Vessia hunting anyone who touches the ledgers. Beat: cold, methodical menace.

chapters.title: An Audit at Knifepoint
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Casserly interrogates Coral under pretense of inspection; Coral lies with ledger-perfect precision and barely survives. Beat: terror managed through craft.

chapters.title: The Map Under Her Skin
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. Ilex reveals she tattooed the erased maps onto her own body to preserve them; the route to the Door runs through her scars. Beat: intimacy and sacrifice entwined.

chapters.title: Debts Called Due
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The collapsing miracle-economy turns the guild's debtors violent; the Thorn burns its eastern wing. Sable must choose between the ledgers and her people. Beat: a leader breaking.

chapters.title: Vessel-of-Thorns Speaks
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Through the cellar door, Coral's god finally speaks—in fragments, revealing the ledgers' lock can only be opened by someone who owes it everything. Beat: reunion laced with terrible terms.

chapters.title: What Coral Owes
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, intercut flashback. We learn Coral sold his childhood memories to the guild to survive; his whole self is collateral. Beat: devastating self-recognition.

chapters.title: The Road Through Unmapped Country
chapters.summary: Ensemble journey chapter. The four set out across terrain that reshapes itself because no map holds it; Pip nearly walks off the edge of existence. Beat: peril bonding them tighter.

chapters.title: A Village That Prayed Too Well
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. They pass a village where every prayer was granted and every villager emptied into smiling husks. A cautionary mirror of the story's question. Beat: horror as moral argument.

chapters.title: Casserly's Sermon
chapters.summary: Casserly's POV. The High Warden captures Sable, offering her absolution for betrayal; her refusal costs her fingers. Beat: antagonist revealed as true believer, not monster.

chapters.title: Rescue Written in Red Ink
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral trades three years of his own remembered joy to buy Sable's release from the Order's custody. Beat: love priced in the currency of self.

chapters.title: Sable Unmade
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Freed but shattered, Sable admits she loved Coral and let him stay ignorant to protect him. Their trust fractures even as the group closes ranks. Beat: love against duty, first wound.

chapters.title: The Door of Unmaking Found
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Following Ilex's tattoos, they reach a cliff face where the Door stands—but it opens only for a name freely surrendered. Beat: awe shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: The Order Closes In
chapters.summary: Casserly's POV. The Silent Order marches with an army of the forgotten—people erased by answered prayers. Casserly believes unmaking the Door will end all miracles forever. Beat: armies converging.

chapters.title: Ilex's Last Survey
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. To hold the route open, Ilex must remain at the map-anchor point, alone, as the army approaches. She says goodbye badly, the way brave people do. Beat: sacrifice accepted without drama.

chapters.title: Negotiation with a God
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At the threshold, Vessel-of-Thorns offers truth: freeing it requires the full surrender of a debtor's name—Coral's, the largest account. Beat: the choice crystallized.

chapters.title: Pip Runs Away
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Unable to bear losing Coral, Pip flees toward the enemy camp intending to bargain with Casserly. Beat: love making children reckless.

chapters.title: The Forgotten Army
chapters.summary: Casserly's POV. Pip reaches the Order and sees the erased people up close—Casserly's own sister among them. Doubt cracks the Warden's certainty. Beat: antagonist humanized at the worst moment.

chapters.title: Stand at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Ensemble battle chapter. The Order assaults the Door; Sable fights beside Coral, Ilex holds the anchor bleeding, and the thornwood door begins to open. Beat: climax ignites.

chapters.title: Casserly's Choice
chapters.summary: Casserly's POV. Confronting Coral, Casserly sees his sister's face among the freed dead-to-be and lowers his blade—then is cut down by his own second. Beat: redemption purchased too late.

chapters.title: When the Thorn Turns
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Climax. Coral speaks his full name into the ledger-lock and surrenders it; the ledgers burn blank, the god steps through, and Coral begins to be forgotten mid-sentence. Beat: triumph and erasure simultaneous.

chapters.title: The God Remembers
chapters.summary: Vessel-of-Thorns' POV (rare divine chapter). The freed god gathers what was surrendered and refuses to keep it—names, it declares, belong to those who earned them. Beat: grace subverting the price.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Miracles
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Vessia stabilizes; gods answer fairly now, priced transparently. Sable rebuilds the guild as a charity of last resort. But Coral is a stranger to her. Beat: bittersweet new order.

chapters.title: The Stranger in the Ledger Hall
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Nameless and unremembered, Coral works as a hired clerk in the rebuilt guild, watching his family from across the room. Beat: exile inside belonging.

chapters.title: Pip's Project
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Pip, who never forgot—not fully, not the feeling—begins secretly recording every detail about the kind stranger, building a counter-ledger of Coral. Beat: stubborn love as resistance.

chapters.title: Ilex Comes Home
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. Surviving her vigil, Ilex returns and recognizes Coral by how he holds a pen—the one thing erasure couldn't touch. Beat: identity persisting through act, not name.

chapters.title: Reading the Counter-Ledger Aloud
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter. Pip reads their records to Coral nightly; each retelling stitches him back together. Sable listens from the doorway, falling for him a second time. Beat: found family as restoration.

chapters.title: The Name Returned
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Vessel-of-Thorns appears in mortal form and offers the name back—with the debt honestly marked, payable over a lifetime. Coral accepts the terms. Beat: grace with accountability.

chapters.title: Signed in Living Ink
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral signs the new contract—mercenary, clerk, beloved—and the ledger hall fills with light instead of blood. Sable takes his hand in front of everyone. Beat: love chosen over duty, duty transformed.

chapters.title: Doors That Open Both Ways
chapters.summary: Epilogue, rotating POVs. One year on: the Door of Unmaking stands open as a gate for the erased to return home; Ilex charts the way back, Pip keeps honest books, and Coral writes the first page of a new ledger titled 'Given Freely.' Beat: peace earned, wonder ongoing.
